import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Quantum unique ergodicity for eigenfunctions of the Laplacian

The **quantum unique ergodicity (QUE) conjecture** of Rudnick and Sarnak (1994) concerns the
distribution of large-frequency eigenfunctions of the Laplace–Beltrami operator on a compact
Riemannian manifold $M$ of strictly negative sectional curvature. It asserts that for *every*
sequence $(\varphi_j)$ of $L^2$-normalised eigenfunctions, $-\Delta \varphi_j = \lambda_j \varphi_j$
with $\lambda_j \to \infty$, the probability measures $|\varphi_j|^2 \, d\mathrm{vol}$ converge weakly
to the normalised Riemannian volume $d\mathrm{vol} / \mathrm{vol}(M)$. The quantum ergodicity
theorem of Shnirelman, Zelditch and Colin de Verdière gives this only along a density-one
subsequence of an orthonormal basis of eigenfunctions.

Mathlib does not yet have the Riemannian volume measure, the Laplace–Beltrami operator or the
curvature tensor. We use the following standard equivalent descriptions.

* The Riemannian volume of an $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold is a positive constant multiple
  (depending only on $n$ and on the normalisation convention) of the $n$-dimensional Hausdorff
  measure of its Riemannian distance. The QUE statement only involves the normalised volume, so
  we use the Hausdorff measure `μH[n]`.
* A smooth function $f$ satisfies $-\Delta f = \lambda f$ if and only if, by Green's formula on a
  closed manifold, $\int_M \langle \nabla f, \nabla \psi \rangle \, d\mathrm{vol}
  = \lambda \int_M f \psi \, d\mathrm{vol}$ for all smooth $\psi$.
* By the comparison theorem of Alexandrov (Bridson–Haefliger, Theorem II.1A.6), a
  smooth Riemannian manifold has all sectional curvatures $\le -\kappa$ if and only if it is
  locally a $\mathrm{CAT}(-\kappa)$ space, i.e. every point has a ball around it in which geodesic
  triangles are at least as thin as their comparison triangles in the hyperbolic plane of
  curvature $-\kappa$. On a compact manifold the sectional curvature is strictly negative if and
  only if it is $\le -\kappa$ for some $\kappa > 0$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Eigenfunction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/eigenfunction)
- [Wikipedia, Quantum ergodicity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_ergodicity)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- Z. Rudnick, P. Sarnak, *The behaviour of eigenstates of arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds*,
  Comm. Math. Phys. 161 (1994), 195–213.
- M. R. Bridson, A. Haefliger, *Metric spaces of non-positive curvature*, Springer, 1999,
  Definitions II.1.1, II.1.2 and Theorem II.1A.6.
-/

open MeasureTheory Manifold Bundle Filter Metric Set Real
open scoped ContDiff Topology

namespace Eigenfunction

section MetricGeometry

variable {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X]

/-- `γ` is a (unit speed) geodesic segment from `p` to `q` in the metric space `X`: it is defined
on `[0, dist p q]`, starts at `p`, ends at `q` and is an isometric embedding of this interval. -/
def IsGeodesicSegment (γ : ℝ → X) (p q : X) : Prop :=
  γ 0 = p ∧ γ (dist p q) = q ∧
    ∀ s ∈ Icc 0 (dist p q), ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 (dist p q), dist (γ s) (γ t) = |s - t|

/-- Consider a comparison triangle in the hyperbolic plane of curvature `-κ` with side lengths
`a`, `b`, `c`, where the side of length `a` and the side of length `b` meet at a vertex `p̄`.
`comparisonCosh κ a b c s t` is `cosh (√κ * d)`, where `d` is the distance between the point at
distance `s` from `p̄` on the side of length `a` and the point at distance `t` from `p̄` on the side
of length `b`. This is the hyperbolic law of cosines, using `cos ∠p̄` as computed from the sides.
(When `a = 0` or `b = 0` the quotient is `0` by convention; this does not affect the value since
then `s = 0` or `t = 0` and the corresponding `sinh` factor vanishes.) -/
noncomputable def comparisonCosh (κ a b c s t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  cosh (√κ * s) * cosh (√κ * t) - sinh (√κ * s) * sinh (√κ * t) *
    ((cosh (√κ * a) * cosh (√κ * b) - cosh (√κ * c)) / (sinh (√κ * a) * sinh (√κ * b)))

/-- A subset `U` of a metric space is a `CAT(-κ)` space (for the induced metric) if any two points
of `U` are joined by a geodesic segment inside `U`, and every geodesic triangle in `U` satisfies
the `CAT(-κ)` inequality: for two points `x`, `y` on two sides of the triangle, `dist x y` is at
most the distance between the corresponding points of the comparison triangle in the hyperbolic
plane of curvature `-κ`. The inequality is stated after applying the increasing function
`cosh (√κ * ·)`. See Bridson–Haefliger, Definition II.1.1. -/
structure IsCATNeg (κ : ℝ) (U : Set X) : Prop where
  exists_geodesic : ∀ p ∈ U, ∀ q ∈ U,
    ∃ γ : ℝ → X, IsGeodesicSegment γ p q ∧ ∀ s ∈ Icc 0 (dist p q), γ s ∈ U
  cat_inequality : ∀ (p q r : X) (γ₁ γ₂ : ℝ → X),
    IsGeodesicSegment γ₁ p q → IsGeodesicSegment γ₂ p r →
    (∀ s ∈ Icc 0 (dist p q), γ₁ s ∈ U) → (∀ t ∈ Icc 0 (dist p r), γ₂ t ∈ U) →
    ∀ s ∈ Icc 0 (dist p q), ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 (dist p r),
      cosh (√κ * dist (γ₁ s) (γ₂ t)) ≤ comparisonCosh κ (dist p q) (dist p r) (dist q r) s t

variable (X) in
/-- A metric space has curvature `≤ -κ` in the sense of Alexandrov if every point has a ball
around it which is a `CAT(-κ)` space. See Bridson–Haefliger, Definition II.1.2. For a smooth
Riemannian manifold with `κ > 0`, this holds if and only if all sectional curvatures are `≤ -κ`
(Bridson–Haefliger, Theorem II.1A.6). -/
def IsLocallyCATNeg (κ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : X, ∃ r > 0, IsCATNeg κ (ball x r)

@[category test, AMS 51 53]
theorem isGeodesicSegment_real (p L : ℝ) (hL : 0 ≤ L) :
    IsGeodesicSegment (fun t ↦ p + t) p (p + L) := by
  refine ⟨by simp, ?_, fun s _ t _ ↦ ?_⟩
  · simp [abs_of_nonneg hL]
  · simp [Real.dist_eq]

@[category test, AMS 51 53]
theorem comparisonCosh_zero_left (κ a b c t : ℝ) :
    comparisonCosh κ a b c 0 t = cosh (√κ * t) := by
  simp [comparisonCosh]

end MetricGeometry

section RiemannianManifold

/- We consider a compact connected smooth Riemannian manifold `M` of dimension `n` without
boundary, whose distance is the Riemannian distance. -/

variable {n : ℕ} {M : Type*} [MetricSpace M] [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) M]
  [IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞ M]
  [RiemannianBundle (fun x : M ↦ TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x)]
  [IsContMDiffRiemannianBundle (𝓡 n) ∞ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
    (fun x : M ↦ TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x)]
  [IsRiemannianManifold (𝓡 n) M]
  [MeasurableSpace M] [BorelSpace M]

variable (n) in
/-- The Riemannian gradient of `f : M → ℝ` at `x`: the tangent vector `∇f x` such that
`⟪∇f x, v⟫ = df_x v` for all tangent vectors `v` at `x`. -/
noncomputable def riemannianGradient (f : M → ℝ) (x : M) : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x :=
  haveI : FiniteDimensional ℝ (TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x) :=
    inferInstanceAs (FiniteDimensional ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)))
  haveI : CompleteSpace (TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x) := FiniteDimensional.complete ℝ _
  (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x)).symm (mfderiv (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ) f x)

variable (n) in
/-- `f` is a (smooth, real valued) eigenfunction of the Laplace–Beltrami operator on `M` with
eigenvalue `μ`, i.e. `-Δ f = μ • f`. This is expressed in weak form: for every smooth `ψ`,
$\int_M \langle \nabla f, \nabla \psi \rangle \, d\mathrm{vol} = \mu \int_M f \psi \, d\mathrm{vol}$.
Here the Riemannian volume is represented by the `n`-dimensional Hausdorff measure of `M`
(a constant multiple of it, which is irrelevant for this equation). -/
structure IsLaplaceEigenfunction (f : M → ℝ) (μ : ℝ) : Prop where
  contMDiff : ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ f
  weak_eq : ∀ ψ : M → ℝ, ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ ψ →
    ∫ x, inner ℝ (riemannianGradient n f x) (riemannianGradient n ψ x) ∂μH[n] =
      μ * ∫ x, f x * ψ x ∂μH[n]

/-- **Quantum unique ergodicity conjecture** (Rudnick–Sarnak).
Let $M$ be a compact connected Riemannian manifold (without boundary) of dimension $n \ge 2$ with
strictly negative sectional curvature, i.e. of curvature $\le -\kappa$ for some $\kappa > 0$.
Let $(\varphi_j)$ be any sequence of eigenfunctions of the Laplace–Beltrami operator,
$-\Delta \varphi_j = \lambda_j \varphi_j$, normalised in $L^2(M, d\mathrm{vol})$, with
$\lambda_j \to \infty$. Then $|\varphi_j|^2 \, d\mathrm{vol}$ converges weakly to the normalised

$$\int_M a \, |\varphi_j|^2 \, d\mathrm{vol} \longrightarrow
  \frac{1}{\mathrm{vol}(M)} \int_M a \, d\mathrm{vol}.$$
The Riemannian volume is represented by the `n`-dimensional Hausdorff measure `μH[n]` of `M`,
which is a constant multiple of it. -/
@[category research open, AMS 35 37 53 58 81]
theorem eigenfunction [CompactSpace M] [ConnectedSpace M] (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    (κ : ℝ) (hκ : 0 < κ) (hM : IsLocallyCATNeg M κ)
    (φ : ℕ → M → ℝ) (μ : ℕ → ℝ) (hφ : ∀ j, IsLaplaceEigenfunction n (φ j) (μ j))
    (hnorm : ∀ j, ∫ x, φ j x ^ 2 ∂μH[n] = 1) (hμ : Tendsto μ atTop atTop)
    (a : M → ℝ) (ha : Continuous a) :
    Tendsto (fun j ↦ ∫ x, a x * φ j x ^ 2 ∂μH[n]) atTop

end RiemannianManifold

end Eigenfunction

This is a positive constant multiple of the Riemannian volume (constant depending only on n and Mathlib's unnormalised convention). Every use is scale-invariant given the L²(μH[n]) normalisation `hnorm`, so the statement is equivalent to the one with dvol. This relies on `IsRiemannianManifold (𝓡 n) M` (the metric is the Riemannian distance).

Eigenfunctions are taken real-valued. QUE for real eigenfunction sequences implies the complex-valued version (split φ = u + iv, both real eigenfunctions, pass to subsequences where ‖u_j‖² converges), so this is equivalent.

Geodesic segments are unit-speed isometric embeddings of [0, dist p q] (`IsGeodesicSegment`); CAT inequality is quantified over all pairs of geodesic segments issuing from a common vertex inside the ball, which is equivalent to B–H's 'all geodesic triangles' formulation (reverse a side to move the common vertex).

curvature is negative everywhere, and let $\Delta$ be its Laplace–Beltrami operator. The
conjecture asserts that for *every* sequence $(\varphi_j)$ of $L^2$-normalised eigenfunctions,

Zelditch and Colin de Verdière, which only gives this conclusion along a density-one subsequence.

Mathlib has Riemannian manifolds (`IsRiemannianManifold`) but not yet the Riemannian volume, the
Laplace–Beltrami operator or sectional curvature. We therefore use classical metric
characterisations of these notions, valid on any smooth Riemannian manifold:

* the Riemannian volume is (a constant multiple of) the $n$-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the
  Riemannian distance, `μH[n]`; the conjecture is invariant under rescaling the volume measure;
* for a smooth function $f$, the Laplacian is given by the mean value expansion over geodesic
  balls (Gray–Willmore),
  $\frac{1}{\mathrm{vol}(B(x,r))}\int_{B(x,r)} f \, d\mathrm{vol} = f(x) + \frac{r^2}{2(n+2)}
  \Delta f(x) + O(r^3)$;
* the sectional curvature is at most $\kappa < 0$ everywhere if and only if $M$ is locally a
  $\mathrm{CAT}(\kappa)$ space (Cartan–Alexandrov–Toponogov), which for a Riemannian manifold
  reduces to the comparison inequality for medians of small geodesic triangles.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Eigenfunction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/eigenfunction)
* [Wikipedia, Quantum ergodicity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_ergodicity)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* Z. Rudnick, P. Sarnak, *The behaviour of eigenstates of arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds*,
  Comm. Math. Phys. 161 (1994), 195–213.
* A. Gray, T. J. Willmore, *Mean-value theorems for Riemannian manifolds*,
  Proc. Roy. Soc. Edinburgh Sect. A 92 (1982), 343–364.

/-- A metric space `M` is *negatively curved* if for some `s > 0` it locally satisfies the
`CAT(-s²)` comparison inequality for medians: every point has a neighbourhood `U` such that for
all `x y p ∈ U` and every midpoint `m` of `x` and `y`, the distance from `p` to `m` is at most
the length of the corresponding median in the comparison triangle in the hyperbolic plane of
curvature `-s²`, that is
$\cosh(s\,d(p,m)) \cosh(s\,d(x,y)/2) \le (\cosh(s\,d(p,x)) + \cosh(s\,d(p,y)))/2$.

For a compact Riemannian manifold with its Riemannian distance this holds if and only if the
sectional curvature is negative at every point and every 2-plane: by compactness this means
$K \le -s^2$ for some $s > 0$, which is equivalent to being locally `CAT(-s²)`
(Bridson–Haefliger, Theorem II.1A.6). In a small geodesically convex ball of a Riemannian
manifold the midpoint `m` above is the midpoint of the unique geodesic from `x` to `y`, and the

over dyadic points of a side gives the comparison inequality between a vertex and every point of
the opposite side, which characterises `CAT(-s²)` (Bridson–Haefliger, Proposition II.1.7). -/
def IsNegativelyCurved (M : Type*) [MetricSpace M] : Prop :=
  ∃ s > 0, ∀ o : M, ∃ U ∈ 𝓝 o, ∀ x ∈ U, ∀ y ∈ U, ∀ p ∈ U, ∀ m : M,
    dist x m = dist x y / 2 → dist m y = dist x y / 2 →
      cosh (s * dist p m) * cosh (s * dist x y / 2) ≤
        (cosh (s * dist p x) + cosh (s * dist p y)) / 2

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Quantum unique ergodicity for eigenfunctions of the Laplacian

The quantum unique ergodicity (QUE) conjecture of Rudnick and Sarnak concerns the distribution of
large-frequency eigenfunctions of the Laplace–Beltrami operator on a compact Riemannian manifold
$M$ without boundary with strictly negative sectional curvature. It asserts that for *every*
sequence $(\varphi_k)$ of $L^2$-normalised eigenfunctions, $\Delta \varphi_k = \lambda_k \varphi_k$
with $\lambda_k \to \infty$, the probability measures $|\varphi_k|^2 \, d\mathrm{vol}$ converge
weakly to the normalised Riemannian volume $d\mathrm{vol} / \mathrm{vol}(M)$. This strengthens the
quantum ergodicity theorem of Shnirelman, Zelditch and Colin de Verdière, which gives this
conclusion only along a subsequence of density one.

Mathlib has Riemannian manifolds (`IsRiemannianManifold`), but no Laplace–Beltrami operator,
Riemannian volume measure or curvature tensor. This file defines these notions from existing
primitives:

* the Riemannian volume is realised as the `n`-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the Riemannian
  distance (`n = dim M`), which is a positive constant multiple of the Riemannian volume; the
  constant disappears after normalisation;
* eigenfunctions of the Laplacian are defined through the weak form of the eigenvalue equation
  $\int_M \langle \nabla \varphi, \nabla \psi \rangle = \lambda \int_M \varphi \psi$ for all smooth
  $\psi$, which on a compact manifold without boundary is equivalent to
  $\Delta \varphi = \lambda \varphi$ for the non-negative Laplacian
  $\Delta = -\operatorname{div} \nabla$;
* the sectional curvature is computed from the Christoffel symbols of the metric coefficients in
  the preferred chart at each point.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Eigenfunction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/eigenfunction)
* [Wikipedia, Quantum ergodicity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_ergodicity)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* [RS94] Z. Rudnick, P. Sarnak, *The behaviour of eigenstates of arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds*,
  Comm. Math. Phys. 161 (1994), 195–213.
* [Sa11] P. Sarnak, *Recent progress on the quantum unique ergodicity conjecture*,
  Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 48 (2011), 211–228.
-/

open Bundle MeasureTheory Filter Topology
open scoped Manifold ContDiff

namespace Eigenfunction

/-
Throughout, `M` is a Riemannian manifold modelled on a finite-dimensional real vector space `E`:
its tangent spaces carry inner products (`RiemannianBundle`), and its extended distance is the
Riemannian distance (`IsRiemannianManifold I M`).
-/

variable
  {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  {H : Type*} [TopologicalSpace H] (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H)
  {M : Type*} [EMetricSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M]
  [RiemannianBundle (fun (x : M) ↦ TangentSpace I x)]

local notation "⟪" x ", " y "⟫" => inner ℝ x y

/-- The tangent spaces of a manifold modelled on a finite-dimensional space are
finite-dimensional. -/
local instance (x : M) : FiniteDimensional ℝ (TangentSpace I x) :=
  inferInstanceAs (FiniteDimensional ℝ E)

/- ### Riemannian volume and the Laplace–Beltrami operator -/

/-- The normalised `n`-dimensional Hausdorff measure of an extended metric space `M`.

When `M` is a compact `n`-dimensional Riemannian manifold whose distance is the Riemannian
distance, the `n`-dimensional Hausdorff measure is a positive constant multiple of the
Riemannian volume, so `normalizedVolume M n` is the normalised Riemannian volume
$d\mathrm{vol} / \mathrm{vol}(M)$. -/
noncomputable def normalizedVolume (M : Type*) [EMetricSpace M] [MeasurableSpace M]
    [BorelSpace M] (n : ℕ) : Measure M :=
  (μH[n] (Set.univ : Set M))⁻¹ • μH[n]

/-- The Riemannian gradient of a function `φ : M → ℝ` at `x`: the tangent vector at `x`
representing the differential `dφ_x` through the Riemannian inner product on `TangentSpace I x`.
-/
noncomputable def gradient (φ : M → ℝ) (x : M) : TangentSpace I x :=
  (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (TangentSpace I x)).symm (mfderiv I 𝓘(ℝ) φ x)

/-- `IsLaplaceEigenfunction I φ l` means that `φ : M → ℝ` is a smooth eigenfunction of the
Laplace–Beltrami operator with eigenvalue `l`, in weak form: for every smooth `ψ : M → ℝ`,
$$\int_M \langle \nabla \varphi, \nabla \psi \rangle \, d\mathrm{vol}
  = l \int_M \varphi \, \psi \, d\mathrm{vol}.$$
On a compact manifold without boundary, Green's formula shows that this is equivalent to
$\Delta \varphi = l \varphi$ for the non-negative Laplace–Beltrami operator
$\Delta = -\operatorname{div} \nabla$. Eigenfunctions of the Laplacian are smooth by elliptic
regularity, so requiring `φ` to be smooth loses no generality. -/
def IsLaplaceEigenfunction [MeasurableSpace M] [BorelSpace M] (φ : M → ℝ) (l : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ContMDiff I 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ φ ∧ ∀ ψ : M → ℝ, ContMDiff I 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ ψ →
    ∫ x, ⟪gradient I φ x, gradient I ψ x⟫ ∂(normalizedVolume M (Module.finrank ℝ E)) =
      l * ∫ x, φ x * ψ x ∂(normalizedVolume M (Module.finrank ℝ E))

/-
### Sectional curvature

The curvature at a point `x₀` is computed in the preferred chart `e = extChartAt I x₀`. A vector
`v : E` is identified with the coordinate vector field `y ↦ D(e⁻¹)_y v`. The metric coefficients,
the Christoffel symbols and the Riemann tensor are then given by the classical coordinate
formulas, using that coordinate vector fields commute.
-/

/-- The metric coefficients of the Riemannian metric in the chart `e = extChartAt I x₀`, at the
coordinate point `y : E`: the bilinear form `(v, w) ↦ ⟪D(e⁻¹)_y v, D(e⁻¹)_y w⟫` on `E`. -/
noncomputable def metricCoord (x₀ : M) (y : E) : E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ :=
  (innerSL ℝ).bilinearComp (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) I (extChartAt I x₀).symm y)
    (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) I (extChartAt I x₀).symm y)

/-- The Christoffel symbols of the first kind in the chart `extChartAt I x₀`:
`christoffelFirst I x₀ y u v w = ½ (∂ᵤ g(v, w) + ∂ᵥ g(u, w) - ∂_w g(u, v))`, that is,
`g(∇ᵤ v, w)` for the coordinate vector fields `u`, `v`, `w`. -/
noncomputable def christoffelFirst (x₀ : M) (y : E) (u v : E) : E →L[ℝ] ℝ :=
  let D := fderiv ℝ (metricCoord I x₀) y
  (1 / 2 : ℝ) • (D u v + D v u - (D.flip u).flip v)

/-- The Christoffel symbols of the second kind in the chart `extChartAt I x₀`: the coordinate
vector `Γ(u, v) = ∇ᵤ v` characterised by `g(Γ(u, v), w) = christoffelFirst I x₀ y u v w` for all
`w`. It is obtained by inverting the metric coefficients; `ContinuousLinearMap.inverse` is the
genuine inverse because `metricCoord I x₀ y` is a linear isomorphism `E ≃ E*` for `y` in the
open target of the chart. -/
noncomputable def christoffel (x₀ : M) (y : E) (u v : E) : E :=
  (metricCoord I x₀ y).inverse (christoffelFirst I x₀ y u v)

/-- The Riemann curvature endomorphism `R(u, v) w = ∇ᵤ ∇ᵥ w - ∇ᵥ ∇ᵤ w` in the chart
`extChartAt I x₀`, for coordinate vector fields `u`, `v`, `w` (which commute):
`R(u, v) w = ∂ᵤ Γ(v, w) - ∂ᵥ Γ(u, w) + Γ(u, Γ(v, w)) - Γ(v, Γ(u, w))`. -/
noncomputable def riemann (x₀ : M) (y : E) (u v w : E) : E :=
  fderiv ℝ (fun z ↦ christoffel I x₀ z v w) y u - fderiv ℝ (fun z ↦ christoffel I x₀ z u w) y v
    + christoffel I x₀ y u (christoffel I x₀ y v w) - christoffel I x₀ y v (christoffel I x₀ y u w)

/-- The sectional curvature of `M` at `x₀` along the plane spanned by the tangent vectors with
coordinates `u` and `v` in the chart `extChartAt I x₀`:
$$K(u, v) = \frac{g(R(u, v) v, u)}{g(u, u) g(v, v) - g(u, v)^2}.$$
It is only meaningful when `u` and `v` are linearly independent. -/
noncomputable def sectionalCurvature (x₀ : M) (u v : E) : ℝ :=
  let y := extChartAt I x₀ x₀
  let g := metricCoord I x₀ y
  g (riemann I x₀ y u v v) u / (g u u * g v v - (g u v) ^ 2)

variable (M) in
/-- The Riemannian manifold `M` has strictly negative sectional curvature: at every point, the
sectional curvature of every tangent `2`-plane is negative. -/
def HasNegativeSectionalCurvature : Prop :=
  ∀ x₀ : M, ∀ u v : E, LinearIndependent ℝ ![u, v] → sectionalCurvature I x₀ u v < 0

/- ### The conjecture -/

/-- **Quantum unique ergodicity conjecture** (Rudnick–Sarnak). Let $M$ be a compact connected
smooth Riemannian manifold without boundary with strictly negative sectional curvature. Then for
every sequence $(\varphi_k)$ of $L^2$-normalised eigenfunctions of the Laplace–Beltrami operator,
$\Delta \varphi_k = \lambda_k \varphi_k$ with $\lambda_k \to \infty$, the measures
$|\varphi_k|^2 \, d\mathrm{vol}$ converge weakly to the normalised Riemannian volume:
$$\int_M f \, |\varphi_k|^2 \, d\mathrm{vol} \longrightarrow
  \frac{1}{\mathrm{vol}(M)} \int_M f \, d\mathrm{vol}$$
for every continuous $f : M \to \mathbb{R}$. Here $d\mathrm{vol}$ is normalised to a probability
measure. Eigenfunctions are taken real-valued; since the Laplacian is a real operator, this is
equivalent to the formulation with complex-valued eigenfunctions. -/
@[category research open, AMS 35 37 53 58]
theorem eigenfunction [IsManifold I ∞ M]
    [IsContMDiffRiemannianBundle I ∞ E (fun (x : M) ↦ TangentSpace I x)]
    [IsRiemannianManifold I M] [CompactSpace M] [ConnectedSpace M] [BoundarylessManifold I M]
    [MeasurableSpace M] [BorelSpace M]
    (hM : HasNegativeSectionalCurvature I M)
    (φ : ℕ → M → ℝ) (l : ℕ → ℝ) (hφ : ∀ k, IsLaplaceEigenfunction I (φ k) (l k))
    (hnorm : ∀ k, ∫ x, φ k x ^ 2 ∂(normalizedVolume M (Module.finrank ℝ E)) = 1)
    (hl : Tendsto l atTop atTop) (f : C(M, ℝ)) :
    Tendsto (fun k ↦ ∫ x, f x * φ k x ^ 2 ∂(normalizedVolume M (Module.finrank ℝ E))) atTop
      (𝓝 (∫ x, f x ∂(normalizedVolume M (Module.finrank ℝ E)))) := by
  sorry

/- ### Tests of the definitions -/

/-- `normalizedVolume M n` is a probability measure when the `n`-dimensional Hausdorff measure of
`M` is finite and positive. -/
@[category test, AMS 28]
theorem normalizedVolume_univ {M : Type*} [EMetricSpace M] [MeasurableSpace M] [BorelSpace M]
    (n : ℕ) (h0 : μH[n] (Set.univ : Set M) ≠ 0) (h1 : μH[n] (Set.univ : Set M) ≠ ⊤) :
    normalizedVolume M n Set.univ = 1 := by
  simp [normalizedVolume, ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel h0 h1]

/-- The gradient of a constant function vanishes. -/
@[category test, AMS 53 58]
theorem gradient_const (c : ℝ) (x : M) : gradient I (fun _ ↦ c) x = 0 := by
  simp [gradient]

/-- Constant functions are eigenfunctions of the Laplacian with eigenvalue `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 35 58]
theorem isLaplaceEigenfunction_const [MeasurableSpace M] [BorelSpace M] (c : ℝ) :
    IsLaplaceEigenfunction I (fun _ : M ↦ c) 0 := by
  refine ⟨contMDiff_const, fun ψ _ ↦ ?_⟩
  simp [gradient_const]

section VectorSpace

variable {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [InnerProductSpace ℝ F]

/-- For an inner product space with its canonical Riemannian metric, the metric coefficients in
the (identity) chart are the inner product. -/
@[category test, AMS 53]
theorem metricCoord_vectorSpace (x₀ y : F) : metricCoord 𝓘(ℝ, F) x₀ y = innerSL ℝ := by
  ext v w
  simp [metricCoord, mfderiv_id]
  rfl

/-- An inner product space with its canonical Riemannian metric is flat. -/
@[category test, AMS 53]
theorem sectionalCurvature_vectorSpace (x₀ u v : F) :
    sectionalCurvature 𝓘(ℝ, F) x₀ u v = 0 := by
  have hg : metricCoord 𝓘(ℝ, F) x₀ = fun _ ↦ innerSL ℝ := funext (metricCoord_vectorSpace x₀)
  have hΓ : christoffel 𝓘(ℝ, F) x₀ = fun _ _ _ ↦ 0 := by
    funext y u v
    have h0 : fderiv ℝ (metricCoord 𝓘(ℝ, F) x₀) y = 0 := by
      rw [hg]
      exact congrFun (fderiv_fun_const (𝕜 := ℝ) (E := F) (innerSL ℝ (E := F))) y
    simp [christoffel, christoffelFirst, h0]
  simp [sectionalCurvature, riemann, hΓ]

end VectorSpace

end Eigenfunction

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Quantum unique ergodicity for Laplace eigenfunctions

Let $M$ be a compact connected Riemannian manifold without boundary whose sectional
curvature is strictly negative. The *quantum unique ergodicity conjecture* of Rudnick and
Sarnak states that for every sequence $\varphi_j$ of $L^2$-normalised eigenfunctions of the
Laplacian, $-\Delta \varphi_j = \lambda_j \varphi_j$ with $\lambda_j \to \infty$, the measures
$|\varphi_j|^2 \, d\mathrm{vol}$ converge weakly to the normalised Riemannian volume
$d\mathrm{vol} / \mathrm{vol}(M)$.

Mathlib has Riemannian manifolds but neither sectional curvature nor the Laplace–Beltrami
operator, so this file uses the following standard equivalent descriptions.

* Curvature. A smooth Riemannian manifold has sectional curvature `≤ -κ` (with `κ > 0`) if and
  only if it is locally a `CAT(-κ)` space (Alexandrov; see Bridson–Haefliger, Theorem II.1A.6
  and Proposition II.1.7 (2)). The `CAT(-κ)` inequality `d(p, x) ≤ d(p̄, x̄)` for a point `x` on
  the side `[q, r]` of a geodesic triangle is written out with the hyperbolic Stewart formula
  for the comparison distance `d(p̄, x̄)` in the hyperbolic plane of curvature `-κ`.
* Laplacian. A smooth `φ` satisfies `-Δφ = λ φ` if and only if
  `∫ ⟪∇φ, ∇ψ⟫ = λ ∫ φ ψ` for all smooth test functions `ψ` (Green's identity; `M` is compact
  without boundary). The Riemannian gradient is the Riesz dual of the differential `mfderiv`.
* Volume. The `n`-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the Riemannian distance, `n = dim M`, is a
  constant multiple of the Riemannian volume. Only the normalised volume enters the
  conjecture, so this constant cancels.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Eigenfunction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/eigenfunction)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in
  mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Quantum ergodicity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_ergodicity)
- Z. Rudnick and P. Sarnak, *The behaviour of eigenstates of arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds*,
  Comm. Math. Phys. 161 (1994), 195–213.
- M. R. Bridson and A. Haefliger, *Metric spaces of non-positive curvature*, Springer, 1999.
-/

namespace Eigenfunction

open scoped Manifold ContDiff
open Bundle MeasureTheory Filter Topology

section Curvature

variable {M : Type*} [MetricSpace M]

variable (M) in
/-- The sectional curvature of `M` is everywhere `≤ -κ`, stated synthetically: every point has a
neighbourhood in which all geodesic triangles satisfy the `CAT(-κ)` comparison inequality.

Explicitly, for `p q r x` in a small ball with `x` on a geodesic segment from `q` to `r`
(i.e. `dist q x + dist x r = dist q r`), the distance `dist p x` is at most the distance from
`p̄` to `x̄` in the comparison triangle `p̄ q̄ r̄` in the hyperbolic plane of curvature `-κ`,
where `x̄ ∈ [q̄, r̄]` with `dist q̄ x̄ = dist q x`. By the hyperbolic Stewart formula, with
`s = √κ`, `a = dist q r` and `t = dist q x`,
`sinh (s * a) * cosh (s * dist p̄ x̄) = sinh (s * (a - t)) * cosh (s * dist p q) +
  sinh (s * t) * cosh (s * dist p r)`,
and `cosh` is increasing on `[0, ∞)`, so the inequality below says `dist p x ≤ dist p̄ x̄`.

For a smooth Riemannian manifold this is equivalent to the sectional curvature being `≤ -κ`
(Bridson–Haefliger, Theorem II.1A.6). The definition is only meaningful for `κ > 0`; for `κ ≤ 0`
it holds trivially, see `sectionalCurvatureLENeg_of_nonpos`. -/
def SectionalCurvatureLENeg (κ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x₀ : M, ∃ ε > 0, ∀ p ∈ Metric.ball x₀ ε, ∀ q ∈ Metric.ball x₀ ε, ∀ r ∈ Metric.ball x₀ ε,
    ∀ x ∈ Metric.ball x₀ ε, dist q x + dist x r = dist q r →
      Real.sinh (√κ * dist q r) * Real.cosh (√κ * dist p x) ≤
        Real.sinh (√κ * dist x r) * Real.cosh (√κ * dist p q) +
          Real.sinh (√κ * dist q x) * Real.cosh (√κ * dist p r)

/-- For `κ ≤ 0` the synthetic bound `SectionalCurvatureLENeg M κ` carries no information. -/
@[category test, AMS 53]
theorem sectionalCurvatureLENeg_of_nonpos {κ : ℝ} (hκ : κ ≤ 0) :
    SectionalCurvatureLENeg M κ := by
  intro x₀
  refine ⟨1, one_pos, fun p _ q _ r _ x _ _ ↦ ?_⟩
  simp [Real.sqrt_eq_zero'.mpr hκ]

end Curvature

section Gradient

variable
  {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  {M : Type*} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace E M]
  [RiemannianBundle (fun (x : M) ↦ TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, E) x)]

variable (E) in
/-- The Riemannian gradient `∇φ x ∈ T_x M` of `φ : M → ℝ`: the tangent vector that represents the
differential `mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ) φ x` through the Riemannian inner product on `T_x M`. -/
noncomputable def riemannianGradient (φ : M → ℝ) (x : M) : TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, E) x :=
  haveI : FiniteDimensional ℝ (TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, E) x) := ‹FiniteDimensional ℝ E›
  haveI : CompleteSpace (TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, E) x) := FiniteDimensional.complete ℝ _
  (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, E) x)).symm (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ) φ x)

/-- The gradient of a constant function vanishes. -/
@[category test, AMS 58]
theorem riemannianGradient_const (c : ℝ) (x : M) :
    riemannianGradient E (fun _ ↦ c) x = 0 := by
  simp [riemannianGradient, mfderiv_const]

end Gradient

section Laplacian

/- Let `M` be a metric space with charts in the finite-dimensional real vector space `E`, with an
inner product on each tangent space and with its Borel σ-algebra. -/
variable
  {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  {M : Type*} [MetricSpace M] [ChartedSpace E M] [MeasurableSpace M] [BorelSpace M]
  [RiemannianBundle (fun (x : M) ↦ TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, E) x)]

variable (E M) in
/-- The `dim M`-dimensional Hausdorff measure of `M`. When `M` is a Riemannian manifold with its
Riemannian distance, this is the Riemannian volume up to a constant depending only on `dim M`. -/
noncomputable def riemannianVolume : Measure M := μH[Module.finrank ℝ E]

variable (E) in
/-- `φ : M → ℝ` is a smooth eigenfunction of the Laplace–Beltrami operator with eigenvalue
`lam`, i.e. `-Δφ = lam • φ`, stated in weak form: `φ` is `C^∞` and
`∫ ⟪∇φ, ∇ψ⟫ = lam * ∫ φ ψ` for every `C^∞` test function `ψ`.
On a compact manifold without boundary this is equivalent to `-Δφ = lam • φ` pointwise. -/
def IsLaplaceEigenfunction (φ : M → ℝ) (lam : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ φ ∧
    ∀ ψ : M → ℝ, ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ ψ →
      ∫ x, inner ℝ (riemannianGradient E φ x) (riemannianGradient E ψ x) ∂riemannianVolume E M =
        lam * ∫ x, φ x * ψ x ∂riemannianVolume E M

/-- Constant functions are Laplace eigenfunctions with eigenvalue `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 58]
theorem isLaplaceEigenfunction_const (c : ℝ) :
    IsLaplaceEigenfunction E (fun _ : M ↦ c) 0 := by
  refine ⟨contMDiff_const, fun ψ _ ↦ ?_⟩
  simp [riemannianGradient_const]

/- For the conjecture, `M` is a `C^∞` Riemannian manifold without boundary: the smooth structure,
the inner products on the tangent spaces and the distance on `M` are compatible. -/
variable [IsManifold 𝓘(ℝ, E) ∞ M]
  [IsContMDiffRiemannianBundle 𝓘(ℝ, E) ∞ E (fun (x : M) ↦ TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, E) x)]
  [IsRiemannianManifold 𝓘(ℝ, E) M]

/-- **Quantum unique ergodicity conjecture** (Rudnick–Sarnak).

Let `M` be a compact connected Riemannian manifold without boundary with strictly negative
sectional curvature, i.e. sectional curvature `≤ -κ` for some `κ > 0`. Let `φ j` be
`L²`-normalised eigenfunctions of the Laplacian, `-Δ (φ j) = lam j • φ j`, with eigenvalues
`lam j → ∞`. Then the probability measures `|φ j|² dvol` converge weakly to the normalised
Riemannian volume `dvol / vol M`: for every continuous `f : M → ℝ`,
$$\int_M f\,|\varphi_j|^2 \, d\mathrm{vol} \longrightarrow
  \frac{1}{\mathrm{vol}(M)} \int_M f \, d\mathrm{vol}.$$

Here `riemannianVolume E M` is a constant multiple of the Riemannian volume; the constant cancels
in the eigenfunction equation and in the normalised limit, and it only rescales `φ j`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 35 37 58]
theorem eigenfunction [CompactSpace M] [ConnectedSpace M]
    (hcurv : ∃ κ > 0, SectionalCurvatureLENeg M κ)
    (φ : ℕ → M → ℝ) (lam : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hφ : ∀ j, IsLaplaceEigenfunction E (φ j) (lam j))
    (hnorm : ∀ j, ∫ x, φ j x ^ 2 ∂riemannianVolume E M = 1)
    (hlam : Tendsto lam atTop atTop)
    (f : M → ℝ) (hf : Continuous f) :
    Tendsto (fun j ↦ ∫ x, f x * φ j x ^ 2 ∂riemannianVolume E M) atTop
      (𝓝 ((∫ x, f x ∂riemannianVolume E M) / (riemannianVolume E M Set.univ).toReal)) := by
  sorry

end Laplacian

end Eigenfunction

sectional curvature, i.e. sectional curvature `≤ -κ` for some `κ > 0`. Let `φ j` be
`L²`-normalised eigenfunctions of the Laplacian, `-Δ (φ j) = lam j • φ j`, with eigenvalues
`lam j → ∞`. Then the probability measures `|φ j|² dvol` converge weakly to the normalised
Riemannian volume `dvol / vol M`: for every continuous `f : M → ℝ`,
$$\int_M f\,|\varphi_j|^2 \, d\mathrm{vol} \longrightarrow
  \frac{1}{\mathrm{vol}(M)} \int_M f \, d\mathrm{vol}.$$

Here `riemannianVolume E M` is a constant multiple of the Riemannian volume; the constant cancels
in the eigenfunction equation and in the normalised limit, and it only rescales `φ j`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 35 37 58]
theorem eigenfunction [CompactSpace M] [ConnectedSpace M]
    (hcurv : ∃ κ > 0, SectionalCurvatureLENeg M κ)
    (φ : ℕ → M → ℝ) (lam : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hφ : ∀ j, IsLaplaceEigenfunction E (φ j) (lam j))
    (hnorm : ∀ j, ∫ x, φ j x ^ 2 ∂riemannianVolume E M = 1)
    (hlam : Tendsto lam atTop atTop)
    (f : M → ℝ) (hf : Continuous f) :
    Tendsto (fun j ↦ ∫ x, f x * φ j x ^ 2 ∂riemannianVolume E M) atTop
      (𝓝 ((∫ x, f x ∂riemannianVolume E M) / (riemannianVolume E M Set.univ).toReal)) := by
  sorry

eigenfunction.why: A faithful statement requires a compact boundaryless smooth Riemannian manifold with strictly negative sectional curvature, its Laplace–Beltrami operator, its Riemannian volume measure, and the associated eigenfunction probability measures. Mathlib has basic Riemannian-manifold/path-length infrastructure and weak convergence of probability measures, but it has no Levi–Civita connection or sectional curvature, no Riemannian volume measure on manifolds, and no Laplace–Beltrami operator (the existing function Laplacian is only for inner-product vector spaces). FormalConjecturesForMathlib supplies none of these. Treating curvature, volume, and the Laplacian as unconstrained input fields would not tie them to the Riemannian metric and would state a different theorem, while defining them faithfully would require substantial missing differential-geometric theory.
